# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five years old  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Origin:** East Grafton  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P44](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0044)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Lavendar is a tiny lady with thick, snow-white hair that is beautifully wavy and arranged in becoming puffs and coils. Beneath her white hair, she possesses an almost girlish, pink-cheeked face with soft wood-brown eyes containing golden glints, dimples, and sweet lips.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002)_

## Personality

Imaginative and romantic, Miss Lavendar retains an inner youthfulness despite her years and likes to populate her seclusion with playful fancies, such as her imaginary 'dream-boy.' Although considered peculiar by locals for living a reclusive life in her isolated stone house, she is warm, hospitable, and sensible, possessing a voice compared to tinkling water and white satin.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P33](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0033), [v2 c21 P35](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0035), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c22 P6](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0006), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029), [v2 c27 P63](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0063)_

## Traits

- Imaginative  <sub>[v2 c27 P63](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0063)</sub>
- Hospitable  <sub>[v2 c21 P42](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0042), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029)</sub>
- Youthful at heart  <sub>[v2 c21 P35](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0035), [v2 c22 P6](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0006)</sub>

## Abilities

- Storytelling and imaginative play  <sub>[v2 c27 P63](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0063)</sub>

## History

Miss Lavendar Lewis lives in a secluded stone house bounded by firs and a garden near West Grafton. Having parted from her former fiancé Stephen Irving after a youthful disagreement, she lived out of the public eye for years, attended by her young handmaiden Charlotta the Fourth. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discover her house while wandering down a secluded lane and are greeted with a warm, festive tea. Anne and Miss Lavendar bond over their mutual love for romance, imagination, and nature, with Miss Lavendar revealing her habit of inventing dream-people to keep herself company. After learning that Stephen Irving's son, Paul, is living in Avonlea, Miss Lavendar eventually invites him to visit Echo Lodge. She quickly forms a fond, special friendship with Paul, sharing games and stories with him. Later, Anne acts as a romantic messenger between Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving, helping prepare for their eventual reconciliation and wedding.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P31](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0031), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c21 P38](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0038), [v2 c21 P42](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0042), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P25](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0025), [v2 c23 P27](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0027), [v2 c23 P34](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0034), [v2 c27 P63](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0063)_

## Background by volume

- Named Lavendar by her father because he fell in love with her mother in a room with lavendar-scented sheets  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Was previously engaged to Stephen Irving twenty-five years ago before a quarrel ended their relationship  <sub>[v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>

## Quotes
